title: theoremC_abstract: BG Appendix C Theorem C as a p/q-level interface lemma over the norm set
intent: State BG Appendix C Theorem C in a p/q-abstract form whose only inputs are oddness of p and q plus the norm-set relation N(2a−1)=1 on E, so any Hypothesis-(B)-style configuration concludes p ≤ q without unfolding the Peterfalvi Section 16 field-normalizer data.

parent.name: theoremC_abstract
parent.statement:
theorem theoremC_abstract {p q : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hp_odd : Odd p) (hq : q.Prime) (hq_odd : Odd q)
    (hrel : ∀ a : GaloisField p q, a ∈ NormSet.normSetE p q →
      NormSet.normN p q ((2 : GaloisField p q) * a - 1) = 1) :
    p ≤ q

applicability.goal_shape: A conclusion p ≤ q for primes p, q whose proof needs only three p,q-level facts about a norm set E ⊆ 𝔽_{p^q}: inverse-closure E = E⁻¹, a size bound |E| ≥ 2, and a root-count step turning those into p ≤ q.
applicability.use_when: the step lemmas are already stated over p and q alone, and a client can supply the boundary hypothesis (here hrel : N(2a − 1) = 1 on E) without unfolding the concrete configuration that produced it.
applicability.avoid_when: the step lemmas still mention the concrete configuration in their statements, or the boundary hypothesis is not what clients hold (so they would have to unfold group data to build it).

consequences: The abstract lemma carries no condition (A) and no Section 16 data, so its obligations are exactly three: the client must supply oddness of p and q and the norm relation hrel. It defers condition (A)'s work to the client that produces hrel (here FieldNormalizerData.normSetGeneratorRelation_of_hypothesisB, line 143); if a client cannot produce hrel without unfolding the configuration, the abstraction buys nothing. Both the inverse-closure and the size bound must be supplied — neither is derived from the other here — so the interface is only as thin as the three step lemmas allow.
